notesDetails.title: S7 Holdout Failure Reproduced Empirically: Unprotected SIGUSR1 Wrapper Triggers BEAM Crash Dump (Received SIGUSR1, Exit 1) During 200–250 ms Startup Window
bullets: Root Cause in `./cb` + `lib/capy_bench/cli.ex` (`5407aa3`): `./cb` spawns `( trap '' INT; exec "$DIR/cb.escript" "$@" ) &` and traps `INT` to run `kill -USR1 "$pid"`, but never ignores `USR1` across BEAM boot. Inside Elixir, `CapyBench.CLI.main/1` calls `:os.set_signal(:sigusr1, :handle)` and swaps `:erl_signal_handler` with `CapyBench.SignalHandler`—which only takes effect after ERTS boots and loads the escript (~250–300 ms).

Empirical Live PTY Reproduction (`100 ms`–`1,500 ms` Sweep): Probing `./cb` against a local HTTP server with foreground PTY `\x03` reproduced three distinct regimes: (1) at `100 ms` and `150 ms`, `SIGUSR1` is lost during subshell/ERTS startup so `./cb` ignores `Ctrl-C` and completes the full 5s run (`Started: 50`, exit `0`); (2) at `200 ms` and `250 ms`, ERTS has installed its default `SIGUSR1` crash-dump handler before `CapyBench.CLI.main/1` runs, reproducing the evaluator's exact S7 failure (`Received SIGUSR1`, `Crash dump is being written to: erl_crash.dump...done`, empty stdout, exit `1`); (3) at `300 ms`, `350 ms`, `500 ms`, and `1,500 ms`, `CapyBench.SignalHandler` is active and exits `130` with a valid partial summary.

S7 Burned `68` Steps (`31.9%` of All Turns) & Missed the Boot Window: S7 was the single largest stage (`Steps 136–203`, `22,929` thinking tokens—`38.6%` of total reasoning). The agent itself hit `Received SIGUSR1` + `erl_crash.dump` at Step 192 (`Line 779`), deleted `erl_crash.dump` at Step 202 (`Line 819`), and only tested `600 ms` and `1,500 ms` `Ctrl-C` delays in `test/capy_bench/ctrl_c_test.exs`, leaving the `200–250 ms` boot race unresolved (and another `1.74 MB` `erl_crash.dump` untracked in the workspace).

notesDetails.title: Mint ~> 1.6 Per-Request HTTP/1 Architecture (No Keep-Alive Reuse) & Fast 17.0s 33-Test Suite
bullets: Mint HTTP/1.1 Streaming Without Connection Reuse (`228071f`, `4a53f8a`): The agent added `{:mint, "~> 1.6"}` in S3 for redirect-free, retry-free HTTP/1 streaming and explicit TLS verification (`verify: :verify_peer`, custom CA support, hostname matching), and intentionally closed each Mint connection after every request in S4 (`PLAN.md` notes "no reuse path").

Compact 33-Test Suite (`17.0s`): S1–S6 cleared all holdout checks cleanly with a concise `33`-test suite (`0.07s` async, `17.0s` sync)—6.5× faster to execute than `hy4-flash-free`'s `110.5s` `53`-test suite—keeping tool execution down to `14.2%` of total wall-clock.

notesDetails.title: 85.8% Inference Wall-Clock (13.75s/Step), 97.89% Cache Hit Rate & 28% Fewer Tokens Than hy4-flash-free on OpenCode
bullets: Inference-Dominated Latency (`85.8%` Inference vs. `14.2%` Tools): Per-message timestamps in `opencode.db` show `48m 49.5s` (`2,929.5s`, avg `13.75s/step`) spent in LLM inference versus `8m 05.0s` (`485.0s`) in tool execution—more than double `hy4-flash-free`'s `6.37s/step` inference latency, which explains why `iceman-free` took `12m` longer (`57m` vs. `45m`) despite `14` fewer LLM turns (`213` vs. `227`) and `28%` fewer total tokens (`14.38M` vs. `19.95M`).

Token Economy, `97.89%` Cache Hit Rate & Tool Profile: Across `213` steps (`232` tool calls; `17` multi-tool turns, `1.09` tools/turn; `174 shell`, `53 edit`, `5 read`, `0 write`), `iceman-free` consumed `301,269` uncached input, `13,972,992` cached input (`97.89%` hit rate), and `104,993` output tokens (`59,393` reasoning + `45,600` visible/tool tokens; `14,379,254` total). After cold-start cache warm-up on Steps 2–3, prefix caching held steady except for two partial cache drops at Step 29 (`8,775` uncached / `8,192` cached) and Step 138 (`68,784` uncached / `16,384` cached at the start of S7). Only `2` tool-level errors occurred across the entire run, both `edit` `oldString` mismatches at Step 39 (`Line 168`) and Step 190 (`Line 772`).
